extracted.intended_audience: developers, researchers, journalists, and members of the public who want to access Federal Register content programmatically or via site search
extracted.subtask_description: Using the FederalRegister.gov API and site search to find, retrieve, and verify Federal Register documents and metadata. Covers legal-status caveats, search behaviors, available endpoints, and input schemas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status disclaimer (prototype vs official edition)
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a 'Web 2.0' version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register, and does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on GPO’s govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register (ACFR) issues a regulation granting it official legal status, the XML rendition on FederalRegister.gov does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts. Users relying on it for legal research should verify results against an official edition of the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document format and link to official PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: The documents posted on this site are XML renditions of published Federal Register documents. Each document posted on the site includes a link to the corresponding official PDF file on govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the site attempts accurate display consistent with the official SGML-based PDF version, users should follow the included link to the govinfo.gov PDF for the authoritative text.

rubrics_metrics.name: OFR/GPO accuracy commitment and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OFR/GPO partnership is committed to presenting accurate and reliable regulatory information on FederalRegister.gov with the objective of establishing the XML-based Federal Register as an ACFR-sanctioned publication in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While every effort has been made to ensure accurate display, confirm important legal or research results against official publications and services (e.g., govinfo.gov or NARA's resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search box and suggestion behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing an item from full text search results will bring you to those results. Pressing enter in the search box will also bring you to search results. Choosing an item from suggestions will bring you directly to the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more detailed background and advanced usage see the Search & Navigation guide linked from the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: API endpoints are public and interactive
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov provides multiple public API endpoints. Each endpoint is detailed below and can be explored interactively by clicking the 'Try it out' button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the interactive explorer on the documentation page to test endpoints and parameters before building automated clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: No API key required; access via HTTP client or browser
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov APIs do not require API keys; all you need is an HTTP client or browser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests can be made directly from scripts, command-line HTTP clients, or browsers without registration; follow endpoint and schema details in the documentation to construct valid requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schemas section lists valid inputs (e.g., agency names)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the bottom of the page in the 'Schemas' section, valid options for various inputs such as agency names are listed in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Schemas section to find allowed parameter values and to avoid invalid requests; use those canonical values when filtering or querying the API.
